subject: Staged prepay + performance collar proposal
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@novumhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing for 2yr staged prepay with seasonality

Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput savings look promising. Procurement asked me to formalize two topics so we can move to internal approval: 1) a 24-month prepay discount that accounts for our seasonal usage swings, and 2) a performance collar (credits) if we materially under-utilize committed capacity in the first 6 months.

To be explicit: Novum expects a big Q1/Q2 spike and a softer Q3/Q4; we’d prefer a staged ramp (40% year-1, 60% year-2 allocation) and a year-end true-up to avoid overpaying for unused tokens. Target discount we had in mind was ~18% for a 2-year prepay with a collar. Can you confirm feasibility (and what documentation you’ll need from procurement)?

Thanks,
Amit Shah
VP Product, Novum Health
amit@novumhealth.com

--

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@novumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for 2yr staged prepay with seasonality

Amit — appreciate the clarity. High level we can support a staged 2-year prepay and a short performance collar. Quick options for you to review: 

- Option A (Balanced): 2-year prepay, 15% list discount, staged allocation (40% year 1 / 60% year 2), year-end true-up, 6-month performance collar that issues pro-rata credits if committed usage < 75% of the first 6-month baseline.
- Option B (Conservative): 2-year prepay, 12% discount, same staging, no collar (lower administrative overhead).
- Option C (Aggressive): 2-year full upfront, 20% discount, limited break clause after 12 months.

I'll loop in finance and legal for approvals — attach a redlineable SOW and an economic model so you can see the math. Which option should I draft for procurement?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Novum Health — request for concession approval (2yr staged prepay + collar)

Team — Novum is asking for a 2-year prepay with a staged ramp (40% / 60%) plus a 6-month performance collar that would generate credits if usage is significantly below baseline. They asked for ~18% discount; I proposed Option A (15%) to start.

Key asks:
- Finance: can we approve 15% off list for a two-year prepay if we include a collar and year-end true-up? Please include any margin guardrails.
- Legal: ensure collar language is tightly scoped (first 6 months only, pro-rata credits, no retroactive downward pricing).

Proposed ramp schedule we’ll present: month 0–3 ramp to 25% of year-1 committed rate; month 4–6 hit 40% year-1 target; true-up at 12 months; year 2 allocation at 60%. We should also include a 30-day notice for material changes and a 12-month early-exit clause for both parties with pro-rata refund/credits.

I’ve attached a quick econ model for review. If finance can sign off at 15% (with the collar as described) I’ll send Option A to procurement.

Thanks,
Ben

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Novum Health — request for concession approval (2yr staged prepay + collar)

Ben — finance review below.

Summary: baseline margin looks OK at 15% discount if the following are true: 1) collar limited to first 6 months and credits capped at 20% of the prepaid amount, 2) year-end true-up is operationalized (we need an explicit usage export cadence), and 3) a 12-month minimum stay or pro-rata recoupment for early exit.

We can stretch to 15% conditional on Legal sign-off of the collar cap and procurement agreement to a quarterly usage reconciliation (we prefer automated export into our billing pipeline). If you want to give 18% you'd need a separate CFO escalation; that moves past standard authority.

Please add a brief clause that caps credits to the prepaid value and includes a simple calculation example in the SOW. Once Legal confirms wording, Finance will sign.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Pricing & Finance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing for 2yr staged prepay with seasonality

Amit — thanks for the patience. Based on internal approvals we can offer Option A with the revisions below: 

Final proposal (Option A - approved):
- Term: 24 months, prepaid.
- Discount: 15% off list applied to prepaid committed tokens.
- Allocation: staged (40% of prepaid value applied to Year 1, 60% to Year 2).
- Performance collar: applies to first 6 months only. If cumulative usage in months 1–6 is below 75% of the 6-month baseline, Redwood will issue pro-rata credits up to a cap equal to 20% of the prepaid amount. Credits apply to future invoices or can be refunded on termination.
- True-up: annual year-end true-up with automated usage export (quarterly reporting required).
- Break clause: 12-month mutual early-exit with pro-rata refund/recoupment.

I’ve attached the redlined SOW and included a worked example of the collar calculation. If this looks good, I’ll prepare the DocuSign and a final summary for procurement.

Link to sign: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=ABCDEFG12345

Best,
Ben

Also, can you confirm whether credits can be applied to Marketplace billing if we route payments through AWS? Procurement asked that specifically.

Thanks — Amit
